notes: Very long functions reviewed by structure: doHardWork (3000 lines), withdrawToVault, withdrawAllToVault, emergencyExit (control flow, calls, storage writes, events, reverts, loops). Source loops: _depositNoFlash while (6014, 9111), _redeemNoFlash while (1630 and 4092 as 'while u > 0' because the borrow target folds to 0 with _borrowTargetFactorNumerator = 0; 5229, 6538, 9587), _liquidateReward for (2902, 7924), _isAddressInList (516, 'while True' with breaks), getAddressArray (506, 536) - all while. Implicit loops (22): receiveFlashLoan IERC20[] decode with per-element address check (942), rewardTokens() encoding, claimAllRewards assets encoding (2846, 7868), and 9 flashLoan(tokens, amounts) encodings as pairs of whiles (3872/3884 ... 10099/10111) - P7 21; where the free pointer is known (2039, 4926) the flashLoan call is printed by name instead. The early 'return' of withdrawToVault correctly runs the updateSupplyInTheEnd tail (4841-4850). currentBalance calls the debt token before the aToken (bytecode order) and subtracts correctly. The fallback 'require calldata.size < 4; require not calldata.size' keeps an implied check (receive only). Event names ProfitLogInReward / PlatformFeeLogInReward / StrategistFeeLogInReward are unknown to the database and their data print as raw memory (counted with P2). P14: 408 'x = mem[_N]' reads of return values. No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful and complete (no aborts), all source loops shown as while, but the four big entry points are long and obscure: calls with raw-memory arguments (P2), Error(string) reverts as raw memory with hex messages, distributed mulDiv fee arithmetic, and flashLoan array encodings left as while loops.
